sourceRhythm.reading: All three one-page scores rendered at 2x and visually inspected. Adopted onsets are from the first bar of versions 1 and 2, repeated twice, not a transcription of either complete exercise. Independent reading pending.

crossCheck.scope: MUS 320 guide gives cyclic intervals 2 2 1 2 2 2 1. Used for bell arithmetic only; its Ghanaian examples are not merged into a Cuban ensemble claim.

notAdopted.reason: The version-3 download shows whole-bar block rests despite the lesson description specifying different left-hand divisions. No block rhythm inferred from that missing notation.

authored.palette: Original procedural Compás bell and stick are audible role proxies, not the MEINL cowbell/block recordings. No sampled lesson audio, bass or inferred conga ensemble.
authored.form: Generic six-part Compás rehearsal form. Intro bell first, then adds block; Verse A uses lesson-one cell; Verse B opens lesson-two doubles in bar two; Chorus uses doubles throughout; Break/Ending expose bell alone; ARP adds an authored last-beat block reply.

boundary: An Afro-Cuban-labelled artist teaching exercise, not a field transcription, complete Bembé, religious service or universal African timeline. It does not stand in for Mixteca yaa sii.
nextGate: Verify actual 48-step board playback, all six conductor parts, 60/96/180 pulse BPM, bilingual screens and resource costs before any promotion; musician review remains required.
